sections.theory:
1. End of unpleasantness (End of Odd Feelings)

Its payment is not unpleasant to taxpayers, because when they buy a thing, tax is automatically paid along with the price, and they do not even come to know that they are paying tax.

2. End of tax evasion (End of Tax Evasion)

Indirect tax cannot be avoided, because when some person buys a thing he pays the tax along with it; its payment is certain.

3. Sense of citizenship (Feeling of Citizenship)

Since indirect tax is included in the prices of things, and poor people too buy those things according to their income, therefore they too get the opportunity to contribute something indirectly to the treasury of the government.

4. Arrangement of equality (Equality)

If such taxes are imposed on items of luxury, e.g. cars, fridges, air-conditioners and televisions etc., then the requirement of the principle of equality can be fulfilled, because in this way rich people will pay more tax and poor people will be saved, because they do not buy such things at all.

5. Wide distribution of burden (Burden Shairing)

One benefit of indirect taxes is that the burden of these taxes spreads over different classes and, like direct tax, the burden does not fall on only one class.

6. Control of narcotics (Control ouer Narcotics)

If indirect taxes are enforced on luxury goods (Luxury Goods), their use and consumption will become less; and the financial resources saved from them can be invested in the production of such goods which the country needs more. As it were, productive resources can be allocated (Allocate) according to need.

7. Increase in savings and investment (Increase in savings and Investment)

Indirect taxes are imposed on the purchase of goods; therefore the quantity of consumption (Consumption) becomes less, and with savings (Savings) increasing an increase occurs in capital formation (Capital Formation).

8. Increase in taxpayers (Increase in Tax Payers)

Indirect tax can be enforced on different kinds of goods and services, and thus an increase can be made in the number of taxpayers.

Demerits (or disadvantages) of indirect taxes (Disadvantages of Indirct Taxes)

1. Regressive characteristic (Regressive)

If these taxes are imposed on things of common need, then rich and poor pay them equally; in this way, in terms of sacrifice, a greater burden falls on the poor, and their nature becomes that of a regressive tax.

2. Lack of certainty (Lace of Certainty)

The income of the government becomes uncertain, because it is not known whether, if tax is imposed on some thing, its purchase will remain as much as before or will become less.

sections.content:
1. End of unpleasantness (End of Odd Feelings)

Its payment is not unpleasant to taxpayers, because when they buy a thing, tax is automatically paid along with the price, and they do not even come to know that they are paying tax.

2. End of tax evasion (End of Tax Evasion)

Indirect tax cannot be avoided, because when some person buys a thing he pays the tax along with it; its payment is certain.

3. Sense of citizenship (Feeling of Citizenship)

Since indirect tax is included in the prices of things, and poor people too buy those things according to their income, therefore they too get the opportunity to contribute something indirectly to the treasury of the government.

4. Arrangement of equality (Equality)

If such taxes are imposed on items of luxury, e.g. cars, fridges, air-conditioners and televisions etc., then the requirement of the principle of equality can be fulfilled, because in this way rich people will pay more tax and poor people will be saved, because they do not buy such things at all.

5. Wide distribution of burden (Burden Shairing)

One benefit of indirect taxes is that the burden of these taxes spreads over different classes and, like direct tax, the burden does not fall on only one class.

6. Control of narcotics (Control ouer Narcotics)

If indirect taxes are enforced on luxury goods (Luxury Goods), their use and consumption will become less; and the financial resources saved from them can be invested in the production of such goods which the country needs more. As it were, productive resources can be allocated (Allocate) according to need.

7. Increase in savings and investment (Increase in savings and Investment)

Indirect taxes are imposed on the purchase of goods; therefore the quantity of consumption (Consumption) becomes less, and with savings (Savings) increasing an increase occurs in capital formation (Capital Formation).

8. Increase in taxpayers (Increase in Tax Payers)

Indirect tax can be enforced on different kinds of goods and services, and thus an increase can be made in the number of taxpayers.

Demerits (or disadvantages) of indirect taxes (Disadvantages of Indirct Taxes)

1. Regressive characteristic (Regressive)

If these taxes are imposed on things of common need, then rich and poor pay them equally; in this way, in terms of sacrifice, a greater burden falls on the poor, and their nature becomes that of a regressive tax.

2. Lack of certainty (Lace of Certainty)

The income of the government becomes uncertain, because it is not known whether, if tax is imposed on some thing, its purchase will remain as much as before or will become less.

3. Pressure of inflation (Pressure of Inflation)

With such taxes the prices of goods become high and the pressure of inflation increases.

Merits (or benefits) of progressive (Progressive) tax

1. Requirement of equality

Progressive tax fulfils the requirement of the principle of equality, because under it tax is collected at a low rate from those obtaining less income and at a high rate from those obtaining more income.

2. Requirement of productivity

Progressive tax fulfils the principle of productivity, because compared with proportional tax the government gets more income from progressive tax.

3. Remedy of unequal distribution

By it the unequal distribution of wealth in society can be made equal and economic difference can be reduced, because on one side, by imposing tax at a high rate on those with more income, enormous wealth can be stopped from accumulating with them, and on the other side, by imposing tax at a low rate on those with less income, or by concessions, their power can be increased.

4. Guarantor of collective welfare

By it an increase occurs in the collective welfare of society, because on one side rich people, because of the imposition of tax, reduce the use of luxuries, and on the other side poor people can fulfil their necessities of life better than before.

5. Elimination of unemployment (Elimination of Unemployment)

With the help of progressive tax help is obtained in ending depression and unemployment. Its working method is this: rich people, by virtue of more income, save a considerable sum, because of which consumption of wealth becomes less, demand falls, and necessary money for buying goods and services is not brought into the market; as a result unemployment spreads. Its remedy is that tax be imposed at a high rate on the rich and, with this money, development plans be promoted. In this way new opportunities for employment will arise in the country and unemployment will be removed.

Demerits of progressive tax (Disadvantages of Prognessive Tax)

1. Unawareness of the correct situation

The principle of this tax is based on many assumptions, e.g. that as the income of someone increases, the marginal utility of the rupee for him keeps becoming less; therefore the rate of tax should be increased. But to know this is very difficult, at what speed the marginal utility of increasing income becomes less, so that the rate of tax may be increased accordingly for people.

2. Difference in economic condition

In it this assumption has been made that if the income of two individuals is the same, then for them the utility too will be the same; but in reality this is not necessary, because it may be that the number of dependants of one man is more and of the other less.

3. Pressure of inflation (Pressure of Inflation)

With such taxes the prices of goods become high and the pressure of inflation increases.

Merits (or benefits) of progressive (Progressive) tax

1. Requirement of equality

Progressive tax fulfils the requirement of the principle of equality, because under it tax is collected at a low rate from those obtaining less income and at a high rate from those obtaining more income.

2. Requirement of productivity

Progressive tax fulfils the principle of productivity, because compared with proportional tax the government gets more income from progressive tax.

3. Remedy of unequal distribution

By it the unequal distribution of wealth in society can be made equal and economic difference can be reduced, because on one side, by imposing tax at a high rate on those with more income, enormous wealth can be stopped from accumulating with them, and on the other side, by imposing tax at a low rate on those with less income, or by concessions, their power can be increased.

4. Guarantor of collective welfare

By it an increase occurs in the collective welfare of society, because on one side rich people, because of the imposition of tax, reduce the use of luxuries, and on the other side poor people can fulfil their necessities of life better than before.

5. Elimination of unemployment (Elimination of Unemployment)

With the help of progressive tax help is obtained in ending depression and unemployment. Its working method is this: rich people, by virtue of more income, save a considerable sum, because of which consumption of wealth becomes less, demand falls, and necessary money for buying goods and services is not brought into the market; as a result unemployment spreads. Its remedy is that tax be imposed at a high rate on the rich and, with this money, development plans be promoted. In this way new opportunities for employment will arise in the country and unemployment will be removed.

Demerits of progressive tax (Disadvantages of Prognessive Tax)

1. Unawareness of the correct situation

The principle of this tax is based on many assumptions, e.g. that as the income of someone increases, the marginal utility of the rupee for him keeps becoming less; therefore the rate of tax should be increased. But to know this is very difficult, at what speed the marginal utility of increasing income becomes less, so that the rate of tax may be increased accordingly for people.

2. Difference in economic condition

In it this assumption has been made that if the income of two individuals is the same, then for them the utility too will be the same; but in reality this is not necessary, because it may be that the number of dependants of one man is more and of the other less.
